Customer to share canonical inference scripts and a 1-hour test dataset by 2025-12-05
Schedule lab run (streaming + non-streaming) for week of 2025-12-08
Jordan to follow up with pricing sketch for Dedicated pilot by 2025-12-09
action_items: Samira: review customer scripts and mark streamable endpoints - due 2025-12-06
Tom: provide target SLA, expected p95 latency and peak concurrency numbers - due 2025-12-05
Priyanka: sanitize and upload 1k sample prompts + 2 reference prompts - due 2025-12-05

summary: Focused scoping on benchmark harness integration. Main goals: agree success criteria (latency p95, accuracy/regression bounds), settle streaming vs non-streaming strategy, get customer scripts onboarded, and schedule lab runs to compare throughput/cost. Customer prefers minimal changes to existing scripts; Redwood offered adapter + example harness. Security and data residency briefly discussed; customer needs SOC2 artifacts and KMS notes.
topics: Workload sizing: concurrency, seq lengths, token distribution
Harness adapter strategy: wrap customer scripts vs rewrite
Security checklist: SOC2, encryption, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Ellis: okay everyone welcome, thanks for making time. quick readout of agenda — align on success criteria, look at sample scripts, and plan lab runs.
[00:18] Priyanka Rao: hi, thanks, we have about an hour, i pulled in our platform and product folks, we mostly care about cost per request and p95 latency, and can tolerate small regressions in quality.
[00:33] Samira Patel: good, can you quantify 'small'? like 1-2% BLEU change or measurables on your evals?
[00:46] Priyanka Rao: um, yeah roughly under 3% change on our intent-classifier accuracy and p95 under 300 ms ideally, or under 500 ms if we can't hit it.
[01:02] Tom Greer: we run a mix of short prompts (avg 24 tokens) and long context summarizations (avg 600 tokens) during peak windows, peak concurrency about 120 concurrent streams.
[01:20] Jordan Ellis: okay that's helpful. for the harness we need representative scripts — are your current callers streaming today or do they call and wait?
[01:33] Luis Mendoza: currently non-streaming, they call and wait for batch responses, but product is pushing for streaming in mobile UI to improve TTF.
[01:45] Marco Li: streaming adds complexity for harness. we can emulate both modes. for benchmarking we typically run: 1) non-streaming at target RPS; 2) streaming with partial chunking to measure time-to-first-token and sustained throughput.
[02:02] Priyanka Rao: what's the expected gap in cost and latency between modes?
[02:12] Samira Patel: depends a lot on model, quantization, and how KV cache is used. rough rule: streaming can improve perceived latency (TTFT) but increases overall compute slightly because of more frequent small token batches. non-streaming often wins on raw tokens/sec and cost.
[02:33] Tom Greer: curious about our quantized LLMs — we've seen 8-bit variants on prem, will Redwood's runtime accept that?
[02:44] Marco Li: yes, we support Q8 / int8 flows and have profiles for fp16/4-bit too, but results depend on kernel availability. we'll surface recommended quantization per model in the benchmark report.
[02:58] Avery Cole: important: we must keep production data out of these tests. can you run the bench with sanitized samples?
[03:06] Jordan Ellis: absolutely. we'll only use the sanitized sample set you share, we can also run a synthetic trace if needed.
[03:13] Priyanka Rao: ok i'll sanitize and upload. how long do benchmark runs usually take?
[03:21] Samira Patel: a basic comparison suite (2 models, streaming vs batch, 3 concurrency points, cold/warm cache) takes roughly 4-8 hours depending on queueing. we're proposing a 1 day lab window to iterate.
[03:36] Luis Mendoza: can you explain cold vs warm cache?
[03:40] Marco Li: cold is when KV cache missed and generation requires full compute; warm is when prefixes hit cache and token generation is lighter. for summarization-heavy workloads warm-cache scenarios matter less, but for chat-like repeated prefixes warm cache improves p95 a lot.
[03:57] Tom Greer: we run both chat agents and long form summarization, so we want both measured.
[04:05] Jordan Ellis: success criteria proposal: p95 latency < 500ms for short prompts and p95 < 2s for long prompts, accuracy regression < 3% vs your baseline, cost per 1k tokens within 10% of target cost estimate. thoughts?
[04:20] Priyanka Rao: that seems reasonable as a starting bar. we'll sign off if lab run hits those.
[04:26] Samira Patel: noted. next — harness integration. do you prefer we wrap your existing python callers, or that we ask you to run a Redwood harness adapter?
[04:38] Priyanka Rao: minimal changes ideally. our callers are async requests in a small wrapper around requests lib.
[04:45] Marco Li: we can provide an adapter that plugs into your call path with two lines of code; also shipping an example async streaming client to mirror your current patterns.
[04:56] Tom Greer: what about telemetry? we need token-level cost breakdowns and latency per route.
[05:04] Elena Ruiz: Redwood console will capture per-request token counts and latencies, and we can expose CSVs or links to dashboards for you.
[05:11] Luis Mendoza: any extra certs or security touches? endpoints must be inside our VPC for the Dedicated pilot.
[05:18] Jordan Ellis: for Dedicated we support VPC peering and customer-managed KMS. we'll send SOC2 summary and KMS integration notes.
[05:27] Priyanka Rao: please send the security docs; procurement will ask.
[05:31] Jordan Ellis: yes — that's one of the next steps.
[05:35] Tom Greer: on load profile — what traffic template do you need? RPS, concurrency, token sizes, error model?
[05:43] Samira Patel: ideal template: timestamps, prompt lengths distribution, concurrency targets, and a small set of reference prompts for quality checks. if you can give a 1k prompt set and a smaller eval set (50-100) we can run both load and regression checks.
[05:59] Priyanka Rao: we can do that. one question — if we choose streaming for production, what are the implications for autoscaling?
[06:09] Marco Li: streaming increases memory footprint per session (KV cache per connection) which affects how many concurrent sessions a GPU can host. autoscaling policies change from token-based to session-based heuristics. we can recommend autoscale rules after the lab run.
[06:26] Tom Greer: are there knobs for batching that behave differently with streaming?
[06:31] Samira Patel: yes — continuous batching must be tuned: batch windows are shorter for streaming (to preserve TTFT) which lowers batch sizes and increases per-token cost; for non-streaming you can use longer batching windows to maximize throughput.
[06:46] Luis Mendoza: how do you handle fallbacks when a Dedicated cluster is saturated?
[06:51] Jordan Ellis: policy-based routing can fall back to a hosted pool or lower-cost model variants. we'll propose fallback policies in the POC plan.
[06:59] Priyanka Rao: timeline check — when can we run the lab? we want results before our Q1 planning (mid Jan).
[07:07] Jordan Ellis: aiming for runs week of 2025-12-08; quick report within 3 business days after runs, then a joint review. fits your timeline?
[07:15] Priyanka Rao: yes, that works.
[07:18] Marco Li: small note — if your scripts depend on streaming hooks (e.g., partial JSON outputs), we need to understand whether you expect intermediary structured outputs or just raw tokens.
[07:29] Avery Cole: mostly raw tokens now, occasional partial JSON for progress updates.
[07:34] Samira Patel: okay we'll include an example for chunked JSON assembly in the adapter.
[07:40] Tom Greer: one more — how do you validate quality regressions in bench? are we running exact-delta comparisons or human eval?
[07:48] Marco Li: we run regression tests on your eval suite (automated metrics) and if margins are tight we recommend a small human review panel. automated metrics first for speed.
[07:58] Priyanka Rao: fine. curious about cost modeling — can we get a per-scenario cost estimate?
[08:04] Jordan Ellis: yes — after we see your prompt distribution and chosen model/quantization we will provide a per-1k-token cost estimate for both streaming and non-streaming scenarios.
[08:14] Luis Mendoza: data retention — will logs from bench contain any PII?
[08:18] Jordan Ellis: logs only contain what you provide; we can mask or redact at ingest. we also offer separate logging retention policies.
[08:26] Priyanka Rao: good. procurement will ask for an estimate for a 3-month Dedicated pilot cost for budgeting too.
[08:33] Jordan Ellis: will include a sketch in the follow-up.
[08:36] Samira Patel: quick recap of technical deliverables: adapter example (async streaming + non-streaming), harness config, recommended batch/window settings, quantization suggestions, run plan.
[08:50] Priyanka Rao: and success criteria as we agreed — p95 thresholds + accuracy bounds.
[08:56] Jordan Ellis: perfect. we'll send the benchmark template and a short checklist for the upload. thanks everyone.
[09:03] Priyanka Rao: thanks all.
[09:06] [meeting ends]
questions: Can Redwood support our 8-bit quantized models?
What are the cost differences between streaming and non-streaming?
How long will the benchmark lab runs take?
Can you run benchmarks without production data?
